newsitem.title: USA: U.S. power prices likely to become volatile -study.
newsitem.headline: U.S. power prices likely to become volatile -study.

text.p: Growing competition among power producers is likely to make U.S. electricity prices volatile, according to a study released on Thursday.

At a time when advocates of competition are trying to entice consumers with the prospect of lower electricity bills, consultants Cambridge Energy Research Associates (CERA) warned that rates might climb from time to time over the next few years, while overall prices would head downward.
"Year to year, there could be price increases," said Gary Simon, senior director of CERA. "This could be one of the things that confounds the public."
